attributes.residual: real 48, insns 79/79, opcode multiset IDENTICAL, every instruction at its target offset. TWO named mechanisms remain. (1) CLUSTER A, the blocker, 2 instructions at +0x20/+0x24: the two independent SDA stores of the function's parameters to lbl_803448AC (level, from r31) and lbl_803448A8 (world, from r30). Target emits AC-then-A8 (descending SDA address, parameter order); ours emits A8-then-AC (ascending SDA address). PROVEN SOURCE-UNREACHABLE by three probes: source statement order, extern declaration order, and both together are ALL exactly neutral -- MWCC canonicalises the emission order of two independent same-type SDA stores and it carries no information about source order, the same anti-tell shape recorded in claim.law.initialised-accumulator-pair-order-selects-register-per-pair. (2) CLUSTER B, a register permutation in the two char_save mask blocks: block 1 (+0x78..+0x98) now matches on base r9 and address r10 but still swaps ours->target r6->r8 (the character load), r11->r6 (the shift amount `bit`), r8->r7 (the constant 1) and r7->r8 (the loaded level_masks[0]); block 2 (+0xc8..+0x100) is still the full permutation, where target coalesces the mask INTO the dying shift-amount register (`slw r8,r6,r8`) while ours writes a fresh r10. NOT A WEBFRANK CANDIDATE: tools/gdl/webfrank_audit.py --grep game/world/tower --min-insns 50 --compact REJECTS with `+0x20: use of g30 does not correspond to g31 under the running renaming` -- cluster A is an operand/schedule swap rather than a consistent renaming, so the fail-closed guard correctly refuses the whole function, and cluster A is source-unreachable, so the machine path cannot be unblocked from source either. Do not hand-author a ranged recolor rule to go around that verdict.
